provenance.prompt: Swarm chapter brief 2026-11-08 (/home/ubuntu/swarm-2026-11/chapter-brief.md); plan/chapters.json row 7; style model plan/models/NOTES.md, the approved Κεφ. 5 and Κεφ. 6; voice Κεφ. 1–4. The withdrawn swarm draft was used as a list of facts only.
provenance.review_required: Codex review (gpt-6.1-sol, high) before commit; owner reads on the live site; text_status stays draft.
notes: G07 licensing: only the four marked previews use a purpose clause (s009 ἵνα, s013 ὅπως, s042 ἵνα in Cyrus's direct speech, s114 the hook ἵνα), per grammar-map licence_levels and NOTES (Κεφ. 6). Purpose ὡς is named in note_en only (with an example built on s009); the four fixed preview lines are ἵνα/ὅπως, so ὡς is deferred to later reading (recorded in OPEN.md). The Cyrus story is narrated in the past, so its purpose clause stands only in Cyrus's own words; the grandfather's fear is a verb + περί (writer_notes). No past-sequence purpose clause, no optative, no fear clause.
G05/G06 forms are used freely (productive from the unit after their target): ἴωμεν (s114), μὴ λίπῃς (s021), μὴ προσέλθῃς (s045), μὴ ἐρωτήσῃς (s059).

New lexeme γέρων (grc-geron) added under the owner's early-basic-words rule (binding brief 2026-11-08): the old shepherd needs a plain name and the word is not planned in any later row. Row 7 records new_lexemes_ceiling 13 (design budget 12). κάτω, σήμερον, κάθημαι, σκιά, ὄπισθεν and ἐσθίω were avoided rather than added (not licensed).

Plan corrections (noted in the row and OPEN.md): (1) the hook keeps «ἐκεῖσε γὰρ καὶ ἡμεῖς ἴμεν» but adds «οὐ μέντοι νῦν … ἡ ἅλως ἡμᾶς ἀναμένει», because the owner's 2026-11-04 ruling moved Κεφ. 8 to later summer after an elapsed interval; 'in a few days' would contradict it. (2) καθίστημι is used for Xenophon stationing the boys beside him (Xenophontic 'post, station') rather than for setting the gifts down, which is a weaker Attic use; ἀνίσταμαι/ἀνέστη is used as planned. (3) The beat's old reaper/farmer of Κεφ. 6 became char-georgos-orous; this chapter's old shepherd is a separate character (char-poimen-geron).

Inner story (Cyr. 1.4.5–11) retold from Xenophon's memory of what Persians told him in Asia (authentic_framing_rule: he has not yet written the Cyropaedia). Adapted [?]: wolves stand for the mountain beasts (bears, boars, lions, leopards in Xenophon); the uncle (Cyaxares) is unnamed 'his mother's brother'; the grandfather's reply follows 1.4.10 closely.

Recurring lines bind chapters: «Μάχεται … ἐν τῷ λόγῳ;» (Κεφ. 6) now answered «Οὔ· θηρᾷ»; «Τρεῖς ἦσαν» (Kleandros, Κεφ. 5) borrowed by Sosias; «Ἵππου ἴχνη ἐστίν» → «Λύκου ἴχνη ἐστίν»; the tied horse (Κεφ. 5) → the tied hound; Sosias keeps the leather piece in his cloak (Κεφ. 5 s054) for Κεφ. 8.

Length: about 1,185 running words against the advisory 680–900 window; over-length is permitted by the owner's binding brief and no scene was padded. Core first uses are below the 20–30 advisory count because the story did not need ἐλεύθερος, ἄρχω, φύω, δύναμις, κύριος, ὅδε, ἀγαθός. After review, χώρα (s036) and κομίζω (s051) were worked into existing sentences so that all of row 7's production words have reading evidence.

Duplicate-sentence warnings are repeated speech tags (ἤρετο ὁ Διόδωρος etc.); Diodorus's repeated «διὰ τί;» is the plan's running joke. Recall warnings for later chapters are advisory scheduling notes for Κεφ. 8–12.

review_questions.question: «Κύρου τοῦ παλαιοῦ» for Cyrus the Elder (Xenophon himself says Κῦρος ὁ ἀρχαῖος in Anab. 1.9.1; ἀρχαῖος is not licensed). Acceptable with the gloss, or prefer another wording?
«Μέσης γὰρ ἡμέρας οἱ ποιμένες τὰ πρόβατα παρὰ ταῖς καλύβαις ἔχουσιν»: plausible pastoral practice (flocks resting near the fold at midday in early summer) [?].
«Μὴ ἐμὲ ἐρωτήσῃς, ὦ παῖ … ἤδη γὰρ τὸ ἄκρον ὁρῶ» — is γάρ natural for Sosias's change of subject ('for I can see the summit already'), or is δέ better?
«ὁ γὰρ κύων ὑφ’ ἡμῶν εὑρεθεὶς ἡμέτερός ἐστιν» read as circumstantial/causal ('since he was found by us'): natural, or would an attributive «ὁ ὑφ’ ἡμῶν εὑρεθεὶς κύων» be clearer?
«τοὺς παῖδας παρ’ ἑαυτῷ κατέστησεν» for 'kept the boys beside him (stationed them)': idiomatic Xenophontic καθίστημι?
«Οἱ δὲ τῶν ποιμένων κύνες εὐθὺς ἐσήμαινον» for dogs barking at strangers (ὑλακτέω is a Κεφ. 8 word); σημαίνω of hounds is the open Κεφ. 3 evidence question.
«ἐκεῖ οὖν τὸ ἔκπωμα ἀποδώσονται» — middle ἀποδίδομαι 'sell' (πωλέω and ἀγορά are Κεφ. 8 words), right beside active ἀποδίδωμι 'give back' (s075, s095): clear enough with the margin gloss?
«Πρὸς ἑσπέραν,» ἔφη ὁ γέρων, «πρὸ τοῦ λύκου.» — answers «Πότε δὲ ἦλθεν;» (s101); is 'before the wolf' clear as 'before the wolf came (that night)' (s074)?
Review cx 1108-104659-6791: σημαίνω 'barked' unverified; popup now reads 'gave the alarm (by barking)'. Evidence question stays open (as Κεφ. 3).

primary_new_grammar.label: Purpose: ἵνα, ὅπως, ὡς with the subjunctive (primary sequence)

cover.alt: High on the far side of a mountain, a few shepherds' huts stand beside a flock of sheep in early summer light. A big brindled hound lies among the sheep. On the ridge above, a man, an old groom, two boys and a mule carrying a cheese and sacks of barley are arriving.
cover.art_brief: Late spring, midday, clear light. View from the summit ridge looking down the far side of a wooded Elean mountain: three or four low shepherds' huts of stone and brushwood by a spring, a flock of white and brown sheep, shepherds sitting in the shade of an oak, their dogs rising. Among the sheep lies a big brindled hound (Thymos), tied by a cord to a tree. On the ridge in the foreground: Xenophon (about 45, short beard, travelling cloak), Sosias (old Thracian groom, grey, leading a brown mule loaded with a round cheese and two sacks of barley), Gryllus (12, red tunic) leaning forward eagerly, Diodorus (10) tired, holding the mule's pack. No other hounds. Painterly, not vase pastiche, no writing.

segments.text: Πρὸ ἡμέρας ὁ Ξενοφῶν ἀνέστη καὶ τοὺς παῖδας ἐκάλεσεν.

inference_aids.gloss: ἀνέστη ← ἀνίστημι ↔ ἔκειτο: πρότερον ἐν τῇ κλίνῃ ἔκειτο, ἔπειτα ὀρθὸς ἦν

segments.text: ὁ μὲν Γρύλλος εὐθὺς ἀνέστη, ὁ δὲ Διόδωρος ἔτι ἐν τῇ κλίνῃ ἔκειτο.
«Ἀνίστασο, ὦ Διόδωρε,» ἔφη ὁ πατήρ· «ταύτῃ γὰρ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ καὶ σὺ ἡμῖν ἕψῃ.»
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

inference_aids.gloss: ἀνίστασο ← ἀνίσταμαι: μὴ ἔτι ἐν τῇ κλίνῃ κεῖσο

segments.text: Ὁ δὲ Διόδωρος ταχέως ἀνέστη, καὶ πρῶτος πρὸ τῆς οἰκίας ἦν.
Πρὸ δὲ τῆς οἰκίας ἡ Φιλησία τὰ ἐπιτήδεια ἐμέτρει, τυρὸν καὶ κριθάς.

inference_aids.gloss: τυρός, -οῦ, ὁ: τροφή, ἣν οἱ ποιμένες ποιοῦσιν

inference_aids.label: τυρὸς καὶ κριθαί
inference_aids.alt: A round white cheese beside a small sack of barley.
inference_aids.art_brief: A round pale sheep's-milk cheese on a cloth beside a small open sack of barley grain; plain light background; painterly, no writing.

segments.text: ὁ δὲ Σωσίας αὐτὰ ἐπὶ τὸν ἡμίονον ἐτίθει.
«Ποῖ πορευόμεθα;» ἤρετο ὁ Διόδωρος.
segments.speaker: char-diodoros

segments.text: «Πρὸς τὰς τῶν ποιμένων καλύβας,» ἔφη ὁ Ξενοφῶν.
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

inference_aids.gloss: καλύβη, -ης, ἡ: μικρὰ οἰκία, ἐν ᾗ οἱ ποιμένες ἐν τῷ ὄρει μένουσιν

segments.text: «Πρὸ ἡμέρας ἀνιστάμεθα, ἵνα πρὸ μέσης ἡμέρας ἀφικώμεθα.»
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

inference_aids.gloss: διὰ τί ἀνιστάμεθα; — πρὸ μέσης ἡμέρας ἐκεῖ εἶναι βουλόμεθα · ἀφικόμην → ἀφικ- → ἀφικώμεθα
inference_aids.reveal_en: so that we may get there before midday

segments.text: «Διὰ τί πρὸ μέσης ἡμέρας;» ἤρετο ὁ Διόδωρος.
segments.speaker: char-diodoros

segments.text: «Μέσης γὰρ ἡμέρας οἱ ποιμένες τὰ πρόβατα παρὰ ταῖς καλύβαις ἔχουσιν,» ἔφη ὁ πατήρ.
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

inference_aids.gloss: πρόβατον, -ου, τό: ὁ ποιμὴν αὐτὰ φυλάττει· «βῆ, βῆ» λέγει

segments.text: Ὁ δὲ Διόδωρος ἄλλο ἠρώτησεν· «Διὰ τί δὲ τυρὸν φέρομεν;»
segments.speaker: char-diodoros

segments.text: «Φέρομεν τυρὸν καὶ κριθάς, ὅπως οἱ ποιμένες ἑκόντες ἀποδῶσι τὸν κύνα,» ἔφη ὁ Ξενοφῶν.
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

inference_aids.gloss: ἑκών = αὐτὸς βουλόμενος
ὅπως … ἀποδῶσι: διὰ τί φέρομεν; — τὸν κύνα ἀπολαβεῖν βουλόμεθα · ἀποδῶσι ← ἀποδίδωμι (δῶ ← δίδωμι): πάλιν ἡμῖν δῶσι
inference_aids.reveal_en: so that the shepherds may give back

segments.text: «Ἀλλ’ οἱ ποιμένες αὐτοὶ τυρὸν ποιοῦσιν,» ἔφη ὁ Διόδωρος.
segments.speaker: char-diodoros

segments.text: «Ἀληθῆ λέγεις,» ἔφη ὁ πατήρ, καὶ οὐδὲν ἄλλο εἶπεν.
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Ὁ δὲ ἐμὸς ἡδίων ἐστίν,» ἔφη ἡ Φιλησία.
segments.speaker: char-philesia

inference_aids.gloss: ἡδίων ← ἡδύς: μᾶλλον ἡδύς

segments.text: Τὴν δὲ Ἀλκὴν καὶ τὴν Ψυχὴν ὁ Σωσίας οἴκοι ἔλιπεν.
«Οἱ γὰρ τῶν ποιμένων κύνες αὐταῖς μαχοῦνται,» ἔφη ὁ Σωσίας.
segments.speaker: char-sosias

segments.text: Ἡ δὲ Φιλησία τὸν Γρύλλον πρὸς ἑαυτὴν ἐκάλεσεν.
«Ταύτῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ οὐ δεῖ σε τοὺς ἡμιόνους ἐλαύνειν,» ἔφη· «σὺ δὲ τὸν ἀδελφὸν φύλαττε.»
segments.speaker: char-philesia

segments.text: «Καὶ μὴ αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ ὄρει λίπῃς.»
segments.speaker: char-philesia

segments.text: Ἐντεῦθεν δὲ ὥρμησαν, πρῶτος μὲν ὁ Σωσίας σὺν τῷ ἡμιόνῳ, ἔπειτα δὲ ὁ Ξενοφῶν καὶ οἱ παῖδες.

segments.text: Ἡ δὲ ὁδὸς πρῶτον μὲν παρὰ τὴν φάραγγα ἔφερεν, ἔπειτα δὲ ἄνω πρὸς τὸ ἄκρον τοῦ ὄρους.

inference_aids.gloss: ἄκρον, -ου, τό: ἐκεῖ τὸ ὄρος ἄνω παύεται

segments.text: Παρὰ δὲ τῇ φάραγγι ὁ Διόδωρος ἔστη.
«Ἐνταῦθα ἦν ὁ ἵππος;» ἤρετο.
segments.speaker: char-diodoros

segments.text: «Ἐνταῦθα,» ἔφη ὁ Σωσίας· «ἐκεῖ δὲ τὸ δένδρον, πρὸς ᾧ αὐτὸν ἔδησαν.»
segments.speaker: char-sosias

segments.text: «Ἀπὸ τῆς διαβάσεως οὖν οἱ λῃσταὶ τὸν ἵππον ἀπήγαγον, ἐνταῦθα δὲ ἔλιπον,» ἔφη ὁ Διόδωρος.
segments.speaker: char-diodoros

segments.text: «Ταῦτα πάντα σοι ἤδη εἶπον,» ἔφη ὁ Γρύλλος.
segments.speaker: char-gryllos

segments.text: «Εἶπες· νῦν δὲ αὐτὸς ὁρῶ,» ἔφη ὁ Διόδωρος.
segments.speaker: char-diodoros

segments.text: Ἔπειτα δὲ ἡ ὁδὸς χαλεπὴ ἦν.
ὁ μὲν Γρύλλος πρῶτος ἀνέβαινεν, ὁ δὲ Διόδωρος ἔκαμνεν.
«Ἆρα πολὺ ἀπέχει τὸ ἄκρον;» ἠρώτησεν.
segments.speaker: char-diodoros

segments.text: «Πολύ,» ἔφη ὁ πατήρ· «λόγον οὖν τινα ὑμῖν λέξω περὶ Κύρου τοῦ παλαιοῦ.»
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

inference_aids.gloss: Κῦρος ὁ παλαιός: πολλοῖς ἔτεσι πρότερον ἔζη, καὶ ὕστερον βασιλεὺς τῶν Περσῶν ἐγένετο

segments.text: «Μάχεται ὁ Κῦρος ἐν τῷ λόγῳ;» ἤρετο ὁ Γρύλλος.
segments.speaker: char-gryllos

segments.text: «Οὔ,» ἔφη ὁ Ξενοφῶν· «θηρᾷ.»
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

inference_aids.gloss: θηράω: διώκει καὶ λαμβάνει τὰ ἐν τῇ ὕλῃ ζῷα, ὥσπερ ὁ κύων τὸν λαγών

segments.text: Ὁ Κῦρος παῖς ὢν παρὰ τῷ πάππῳ ἐν τῇ τῶν Μήδων χώρᾳ ἔμενεν.
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

inference_aids.gloss: πάππος, -ου, ὁ: ὁ τῆς μητρὸς πατήρ (ἢ ὁ τοῦ πατρός)
χώρα, -ας, ἡ = γῆ: ἐν τῇ γῇ, ἐν ᾗ οἱ Μῆδοι οἰκοῦσιν
inference_aids.reveal_en: in the land of the Medes

segments.text: ὁ δὲ πάππος, Ἀστυάγης ὀνόματι, παράδεισον μέγαν εἶχεν.
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

inference_aids.gloss: παράδεισος, -ου, ὁ: χωρίον μέγα, καὶ τεῖχος περὶ αὐτό· ἐν αὐτῷ ζῷα τρέφεται

inference_aids.alt: Inner story: the boy Cyrus, richly dressed in Median clothes, sits on a horse at the open gate of a walled game park; beyond the gate the wooded mountains rise. His grandfather, an old king, stands at the gate watching him, uneasy; horsemen wait behind the boy.
inference_aids.art_brief: Inner story (told by Xenophon on the climb). Media, morning. A walled royal game park (low stone wall, a wooden gate standing open); inside, open parkland with a few deer far off. At the gate the boy Cyrus (about twelve, beardless, in a richly coloured Median coat and trousers, a javelin in hand) sits a bay horse, looking out eagerly towards wooded mountains. His grandfather Astyages (old, grey-bearded, in a long royal robe and tall cap) stands at the gate with one hand raised, watching him with worry. Behind the boy: a young man (his mother's brother) and several horsemen with spears. No wolves visible. Painterly, not vase pastiche, no writing.

segments.text: ἐν δὲ τῷ παραδείσῳ πολλὰ θηρία ἦν, καὶ ὁ Κῦρος αὐτὰ ἐθήρα.
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

inference_aids.gloss: θηρίον ↔ πρόβατον: τὸ μὲν θηρίον τὸν ἄνθρωπον φεύγει, τὸ δὲ πρόβατον αὐτῷ ἕπεται
ἐθήρα ← θηράω (θηρᾷ)

segments.text: Ταχέως δὲ ὀλίγα ἔτι θηρία ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ ἐλείπετο.
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Ταῦτα μὲν τὰ θηρία ὀλίγα ἐστὶ καὶ μικρά,» ἔφη ὁ Κῦρος· «ἐν δὲ τοῖς ὄρεσι πολλὰ καὶ μεγάλα.»
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: Ἔπειτα δὲ πρὸς τὸν πάππον ἦλθεν.
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Ἄφες με, ὦ πάππε,» ἔφη, «ἵνα θηρῶ τὰ ἐν τοῖς ὄρεσι θηρία.»
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

inference_aids.gloss: ἄφες ← ἀφίημι: ἔασόν με ἀπελθεῖν
διὰ τί; — θηρᾶν βούλεται

segments.text: Ὁ δὲ πάππος περὶ τοῦ παιδὸς ἐφοβεῖτο· ἐν γὰρ τοῖς ὄρεσι καὶ λύκοι ἦσαν.
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

inference_aids.gloss: λύκος, -ου, ὁ: θηρίον ὅμοιον κυνί, ὃ τὰ πρόβατα ἀποκτείνει

segments.text: ὅμως δὲ αὐτὸν ἔπεμψε σὺν τῷ τῆς μητρὸς ἀδελφῷ καὶ ἱππεῦσι πολλοῖς.
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Τοῖς μεγάλοις θηρίοις μὴ προσέλθῃς,» ἔλεγον οἱ ἱππεῖς· «τὰ δὲ μικρὰ δίωκε.»
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: Ἐν δὲ τῷ ὄρει θηρίον τι ἐκ τῆς ὕλης ἔφυγεν.
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: ὁ δὲ Κῦρος οὐκέτι ἐνεθυμεῖτο ἃ οἱ ἱππεῖς ἔλεγον, ἀλλ’ εὐθὺς ἐδίωκεν.
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: ὁ δὲ ἵππος αὐτοῦ ἔπεσεν, καὶ ὁ Κῦρος ἐκινδύνευσε καὶ αὐτὸς πεσεῖν.
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ τοῦ ἵππου ἔμεινε, καὶ τὸ θηρίον καταλαβὼν ἀπέκτεινεν.
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Εὖ γε!» ἐβόησεν ὁ Γρύλλος.
segments.speaker: char-gryllos

segments.text: Ὁ δὲ Κῦρος τὰ θηρία οἴκαδε ἐκόμισε καὶ τῷ πάππῳ δῶρα ἔδωκεν.
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

inference_aids.gloss: ἐκόμισε ← κομίζω: ἤνεγκε, φέρων ἤγαγεν
δῶρον, -ου, τό: ὃ φίλος φίλῳ δίδωσιν ἄνευ ἀργυρίου

segments.text: «Δέχομαι μὲν τὰ δῶρα, ὦ παῖ,» ἔφη ὁ πάππος· «σὲ δὲ κινδυνεύειν οὐ βούλομαι.»
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

inference_aids.gloss: δέχομαι ↔ δίδωμι: σὺ δίδως, ἐγὼ δέχομαι

segments.text: «Ἐγὼ ὥσπερ ὁ Κῦρος,» ἔφη ὁ Γρύλλος· «ἐν γὰρ τοῖς ὄρεσι θηρᾶν βούλομαι.»
segments.speaker: char-gryllos

segments.text: «Ἐγὼ δὲ ὥσπερ ὁ πάππος,» ἔφη ὁ Ξενοφῶν.
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Πόθεν τοῦτον τὸν λόγον οἶσθα;» ἤρετο ὁ Διόδωρος.
segments.speaker: char-diodoros

segments.text: «Ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ ἤκουσα,» ἔφη ὁ πατήρ· «οἱ γὰρ Πέρσαι πολλὰ περὶ Κύρου λέγουσιν.»
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ; λέγε δὴ καὶ τὰ ἐκεῖ, ὦ πάτερ!» ἔφη ὁ Γρύλλος.
segments.speaker: char-gryllos

segments.text: «Τὸν Σωσίαν ἐρώτα,» ἔφη ὁ Ξενοφῶν.
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Μὴ ἐμὲ ἐρωτήσῃς, ὦ παῖ,» ἔφη ὁ Σωσίας· «ἤδη γὰρ τὸ ἄκρον ὁρῶ.»
segments.speaker: char-sosias

grammar.title: Διὰ τί; — Ἵνα …
grammar.rule: διὰ τί ἀνιστάμεθα; — ἵνα ἀφικώμεθα · διὰ τί φέρομεν; — ὅπως ἀποδῶσι · ἄφες με, ἵνα θηρῶ · ἴωμεν, ἵνα εὕρωμεν

tables.caption: purpose clauses in this chapter: the main verb is present, imperative or hortatory
rows: «Πρὸ ἡμέρας ἀνιστάμεθα, ἵνα πρὸ μέσης ἡμέρας ἀφικώμεθα.» (s009)
We get up before daybreak so that we may arrive before midday.
«Φέρομεν τυρὸν καὶ κριθάς, ὅπως οἱ ποιμένες ἑκόντες ἀποδῶσι τὸν κύνα.» (s013)
We are bringing cheese and barley so that the shepherds may give the dog back willingly.
«Ἄφες με, ὦ πάππε, ἵνα θηρῶ τὰ ἐν τοῖς ὄρεσι θηρία.» (s042)
Let me go, grandfather, so that I may hunt the animals in the mountains.
«Ἴωμεν εἰς Ὀλυμπίαν, ἵνα τοὺς λῃστὰς εὕρωμεν.» (s114)
Let's go to Olympia so that we may find the robbers.

tables.caption: the subjunctive in each purpose clause
rows: α + ω → ῶ: the same as the indicative; ἵνα shows the mood
-μι verb (δῶ ← δίδωμι, Κεφ. 5): read it, do not make it yet

grammar.note_en:
A purpose clause answers the question διὰ τί; "why? what for?". Diodorus asks it at every turn this morning, and his father answers with ἵνα or ὅπως "so that, in order that" and a verb in the subjunctive.

«Πρὸ ἡμέρας ἀνιστάμεθα, ἵνα πρὸ μέσης ἡμέρας ἀφικώμεθα.» "We get up before daybreak so that we may arrive before midday" (s009).
«Φέρομεν τυρὸν καὶ κριθάς, ὅπως οἱ ποιμένες ἑκόντες ἀποδῶσι τὸν κύνα.» "We are bringing cheese and barley so that the shepherds may give the dog back willingly" (s013).
Cyrus to his grandfather: «Ἄφες με, ὦ πάππε, ἵνα θηρῶ τὰ ἐν τοῖς ὄρεσι θηρία.» "Let me go, grandfather, so that I may hunt the animals in the mountains" (s042).
Gryllus at the end: «Ἴωμεν εἰς Ὀλυμπίαν, ἵνα τοὺς λῃστὰς εὕρωμεν.» "Let's go to Olympia so that we may find the robbers" (s114).

ἵνα and ὅπως mean the same here; Xenophon likes ὅπως. A third word, ὡς, is used in the same way (ὡς ἀφικώμεθα = ἵνα ἀφικώμεθα); this chapter does not use it, and you will meet it in later reading. The negative is μή: ἵνα μὴ … "so that … not", "lest …". English often turns these into an infinitive ("we get up early to arrive before midday"), and the margin glosses do the same in Greek: διὰ τί φέρομεν; — τὸν κύνα ἀπολαβεῖν βουλόμεθα. But Greek prefers the clause whenever the purpose has its own subject: the shepherds are to give the dog back, not we.

The mood. The subjunctive here does not say that anything will happen, only that it is wanted. Aspect works as in the hortatory subjunctive of Κεφάλαιον 5: the aorist (ἀφικώμεθα, εὕρωμεν, ἀποδῶσι) for one act seen whole, the present (θηρῶ) for an activity that goes on; neither is past. Build the aorist from the aorist stem without augment: ἀφικόμην → ἀφικ- → ἀφικώμεθα; ηὗρον → εὑρ- → εὕρωμεν. θηρῶ is the present subjunctive of θηράω, contracted from θηράω; it looks exactly like the indicative "I hunt", and only ἵνα tells you which it is. ἀποδῶσι belongs to the -μι verbs (δῶ ← δίδωμι, Κεφ. 5): read it now and leave making it for later.

Primary sequence only. Every main verb above is present (ἀνιστάμεθα, φέρομεν), an imperative (ἄφες) or a hortatory subjunctive (ἴωμεν): the purpose looks forward from now. After a past main verb Greek can put the purpose clause in the optative, though the subjunctive also remains possible; this course postpones that contrast (optative forms in Κεφάλαιον 9, this use in Κεφάλαιον 11). That is why the Cyrus story, told in the past, keeps its purpose clause inside Cyrus's own words, and why the narrator says only that the grandfather was afraid for the boy (s043) and sent him out anyway.

Two other things that look similar. μή with a second-person aorist subjunctive in a main clause is a prohibition, not a purpose: Philesia's «Καὶ μὴ αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ ὄρει λίπῃς» "And don't leave him on the mountain" (s021). And a wish is not a purpose clause, though it can explain why someone acts: βούλομαι + infinitive says what someone wants to do, «ἐν γὰρ τοῖς ὄρεσι θηρᾶν βούλομαι» "for I want to hunt in the mountains" (s053). When you meet ἵνα or ὅπως, look for the subjunctive a few words on, and translate "so that … may …" or "to …".

parergon.title: λαβών, λύσας, εὑρεθείς
parergon.body_en: The active aorist participles here are built on the aorist stem, without augment, and end in -ών (second aorist) or -ας (first aorist): ἔλαβον → λαβών, λαβόντος; ἔλυσα → λύσας, λύσαντος. Each describes one completed act before or alongside the main verb: «λαβὼν … ἔθηκεν» 'he took … and put it down' (s083). The aorist passive participle ends in -είς, -έντος: εὑρεθείς 'found' (s071). -μενος marks middle or passive forms; the stem shows the tense. Here κείμενοι 'lying' (s068) is present middle; λαβών and λύσας are active aorist, εὑρεθείς passive aorist.

rows: λαβών, λαβόντος (ἔλαβον, λαβ-): «τὸν τυρὸν … λαβὼν … ἔθηκεν» (s083)
taking / having taken the cheese, he put it down
he caught the animal and killed it
λύσας, λύσαντος (ἔλυσα, λυσ-): «τὸν Θυμὸν λύσας ἀφῆκεν» (s094)
he untied Thymos and let him go

pair.sense_grc: ἀνίσταμαι, ἀνέστη: ὀρθὸς γίγνομαι ↔ κεῖμαι: οἱ ποιμένες κείμενοι ἀνίσταντο
pair.sense_en: (middle, and aorist ἀνέστη) stand up, get up

pair.sense_grc: καθίστημι, κατέστησα: ἄλλον ἐκεῖ ἵστημι: ὁ Ξενοφῶν τοὺς παῖδας παρ’ ἑαυτῷ κατέστησεν
pair.sense_en: set (someone) in a place, station; (later) appoint, establish

families.spelling_note: ἀνα- + ἵστημι → ἀν-ίστημι: ἀνά loses its last vowel before the vowel of ἵστημι, and the augment comes after the preverb: ἀν-έ-στη 'he stood up' (s069). κατα- + ἵστημι → κατ’ + ἵστημι → καθ-ίστημι: κατά loses its vowel, and its τ becomes θ before the rough breathing of ἵστημι, as in καθ’ ἡμέραν. In the aorist the augment ε has no rough breathing, so the τ stays: κατ-έ-στησεν (s064). ἀνα- is 'up', and ἀνίσταμαι is what the shepherds do when they get up from lying under a tree (s068): the subject stands up. κατα- is not 'down' here: καθίστημι means 'make (someone else) stand in a place, station', as a general posts his men, and later 'appoint, establish, bring into a state'. So the shepherds ἀνίσταντο, themselves; Xenophon κατέστησε the boys, when Gryllus would rather have run to Thymos.

diagram.alt: Two panels. Left, labelled ἀνίσταται: a shepherd who was sitting on a stone rises to his feet; an arrow points straight up beside him. Right, labelled καθίστησι: a man in a cloak sets two boys in place behind him with an outstretched arm; a curved arrow runs from the boys' old position to the place behind him.
